newsitem.title: UK: Brit Borneo gains more as bid talk lingers.
newsitem.headline: Brit Borneo gains more as bid talk lingers.

text.p: Shares in British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc on Tuesday extended their morning gains, fuelled by persistent hopes the oil exploration minnow would attract a takeover bid, analysts said.
British-Borneo, one of the best performing shares on the London stock exchange so far this year, advanced 55 pence to 1,412-1/2 after they already added 347-1/2 pence on Monday.
Bid hopes flared up following a weekend press report, saying Britain's biggest exploration and production firm Enterprise Oil Plc might make an acquisition this year of up to one billion stg.
Enterprise, which traded down 12-1/2 pence to 624-1/2, has been frequently touted as a potential bidder for British Borneo, which has powered 76 percent ahead since the start of the year.
Enterprise, which will release its 1996 results on Thursday, last year concluded an alliance with Pennzoil Co for operations in the Gulf of Mexico -- the oil industry's current hot spot.

British Borneo, which currently has a market capitalisation of 866.2 million stg, is also active there, developing the promising Morpeth field, which is scheduled to come onstream in the summer of 1998.
Morpeth is estimated to have proven and probable reserves of 77 million barrels of oil equivalent.

Confirming the Gulf of Mexico's attractions, Exxon Corp on Monday announced it and British Petroleum Co Plc had discovered deepwater reserves which might exceed 100 million barrels of oil equivalent off Texas.
News of the find initially helped BP, but shares in the oil giant later retreated on the back of weak crude oil prices, trading four pence lower at 713.
